title: Proposition 2: generalized CLP separated-polynomial rank bound
statement_scope: For a finite field F_q, a subset A of F_q^n, elements alpha, beta, gamma of F_q with alpha+beta+gamma=0, and real d in [0,2n], if P in S_n^d satisfies P(alpha a+beta b)=0 for every pair a,b of distinct elements of A, then the number of a in A for which P(-gamma a) is nonzero is at most 2 m_(d/2). The proposition permits gamma=0; no gamma-nonzero condition is imported from the main theorem.

standard_prerequisites: Linear algebra over a field: a sum of r rank-one matrices has rank at most r; a diagonal matrix has rank equal to the number of its nonzero diagonal entries.

Two-block polynomial expansion: a polynomial of total degree at most d in alpha x + beta y expands as a finite sum of products m(x)m'(y) with deg(m)+deg(m') at most d, hence at least one factor in each summand has degree at most d/2.
Finite fields and polynomial rings; the source-local notation M_n, S_n, S_n^d and m_d is defined at lines 171-176 and is retained as context.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Generalized Croot-Lev-Pach polynomial separation: expand P(alpha x+beta y) into two sums each separating a monomial of degree at most d/2, then bound the rank of the evaluation matrix B_ab=P(alpha a+beta b) by 2m_(d/2); diagonality from the vanishing hypothesis gives the nonzero-value bound.

Different hypotheses, quantifiers and conclusion; the main theorem uses this proposition.

Concerns complete 3-AP-free sets in F_p^n and the asymptotic upper bound a(3-AP,F_p^n) <= C n^(1+epsilon) p^(n/2). It has no polynomial P in S_n^d, no alpha/beta/gamma, no A x A rank argument and no 2 m_(d/2) conclusion. Different object and theorem.

Concerns completeness of the subgroup of d-th powers in F_q^* for representing elements by distinct elements summing to zero. It has no subset A of F_q^n, no polynomial degree space and no rank bound. Different hypotheses and conclusion.

Its proposition proves that a product of (1,-1)-saturating sets in F_q^m and F_q^n is (1,-1)-saturating. The hypotheses and conclusion are product saturation, not polynomial vanishing on A x A or a 2 m_(d/2) nonzero-value bound.

An analytic estimate for sums of multiplicative characters of linear forms over F_p^m, with a character-sum bound. The object is character sums rather than a polynomial P in S_n^d and the conclusion is not a rank/diagonal bound of 2 m_(d/2).
